mount-gower.name: Mount Gower
mount-gower.bio: Lord Howe's 875 m summit, reached only with a licensed guide on an eight-hour trek with rope-assisted climbs.
mount-gower.hours: Guided tours only; book ahead (about 8 hours return)
notes: Guided-only per LHI Board walking-tracks page; sold by several operators (Lord Howe Environmental Tours, Sea to Summit Expeditions) so no ticketUrl.
A$200 is the undated Lord Howe Environmental Tours price from the tourism association listing; other operators' prices and guiding months not found.
Summit pin (OSM peak). Guide route midpoint -31.5725,159.07417 if a route pin is preferred.
Photo candidate: Mount Gower, Lord Howe Island, NSW, Australia.jpg, hero_crop x 0.5 y 0.4 (Lens to confirm).

balls-pyramid.name: Ball's Pyramid
balls-pyramid.bio: The world's tallest sea stack, 551 m high and 23 km offshore, reached only by boat tour or dive trip.
balls-pyramid.hours: Boat tours and dive trips by booking, weather permitting
notes: No ticketUrl: sold by many operators (Reef N Beyond, Dive Lord Howe, Belle Chase, Sea Lord Howe).
A$250 is Reef N Beyond's 'from' price for the 3.5 hour expedition; dive and fishing-charter prices differ (Belle Chase fishing A$450). Dive Lord Howe runs September to May.
Distance: 23 km per tourism board and Wikipedia; Belle Chase says 15 km, Wikipedia's diving paragraph 26 km. Recreational climbing is prohibited (stick insect habitat).
Coordinates are the Wikipedia sea-stack point, correct for an offshore feature.
Photo candidate: Balls Pyramid, Lord Howe Marine Park 1008.jpg (licence to confirm).

neds-beach.name: Ned's Beach
neds-beach.bio: A calm north-east beach where you wade in to hand-feed fish and snorkel over a fringing coral reef.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach, no single steward.
Fish food ($1 coin) and snorkel hire (honesty box) are optional extras, not an entry cost.
Photo: weak accept on Neds Beach.jpg; compare 'Lord Howe Island Ned's Beach.jpg'.

malabar-hill.name: Malabar Hill
malabar-hill.bio: A two-hour return climb from Ned's Beach to cliff views and courting red-tailed tropicbirds, September to May.
notes: No ticketUrl: walking track, no single steward.
Summit pin (OSM peak); Ned's Beach to summit route midpoint would be -31.51856,159.06190.
Wikivoyage calls it the island's most popular walk. No closure found, but current track status was not confirmed.
wiki title taken from research wiki_title; confirm the article exists before shipping.

old-settlement-beach.name: Old Settlement Beach
old-settlement-beach.bio: Weather-sculpted sandstone rocks dot the south end of this beach, where turtles are often seen close to shore.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach, no single steward.
Bio fixed: old 'southern beach' was wrong (the source's 'southern end' is the beach's own south end); turtles best at mid to high tide.
No passing Commons photo; needs a search outside Commons.

blinky-beach.name: Blinky Beach
blinky-beach.bio: An unspoilt west-coast beach for surfing and swimming, reached on foot from Transit Hill or Lagoon Road.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach, no single steward.
Bio fixed: dropped unsourced 'picnic area'. Surf hazard and lifeguard status not found.
Transit Hill track is steep and slippery when wet.
Photo candidate: Blinky Beach - panoramio.jpg (Lens to confirm it is Blinky).

north-bay-lord-howe.name: North Bay
north-bay-lord-howe.bio: A secluded north beach reached only on foot or by boat, with snorkelling over the wreck of the Favourite.
north-bay-lord-howe.hours: Open 24 hours (Mt Eliza track closed 1 September to 1 March)
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach; boat access sold by several operators.
Coordinate is an approximate centroid (OSM names it 'North Beach'); track end -31.5165,159.0448.
Mt Eliza closure confirmed for 2025-26; 2026-27 notice not seen. Beach itself is open.
Picnic area has toilets and barbecues. Photo is only a candidate/review (check 1 unproven).

intermediate-hill-lord-howe.name: Intermediate Hill
intermediate-hill-lord-howe.bio: A steep 1 km climb to a 250 m summit platform with views across the island to Ball's Pyramid.
notes: No ticketUrl: walking track, no single steward.
Board lists 1 km one way, moderate; Wikipedia lists 45 minutes return. No seasonal closure found.

transit-hill-lord-howe.name: Transit Hill
transit-hill-lord-howe.bio: An easy 1.2 km walk from the Administration Office to a summit lookout with a 360-degree view.
notes: No ticketUrl: walking track, no single steward.
Return takes about an hour per the tourism board; Wikipedia says 2 km, 2 hours return. Can return via Blinky Beach.
No Commons photo; needs a search outside Commons.

muttonbird-point.name: Muttonbird Point
muttonbird-point.bio: A lookout platform on a short side track off the coastal walk, with views across to Muttonbird Point.
notes: No ticketUrl: lookout on a public track.
Bio fixed: unsourced seabird colony and blowhole removed.
Sidetrack is about 1.4 km along the coastal track to Boat Harbour from Lagoon Road. Arguably part of that track (COVERAGE 'part of a larger spot'); owner may review.
wiki title from research wiki_title; confirm the article exists before shipping.

goat-house-cave.name: Goat House Cave
goat-house-cave.bio: A difficult 2.1 km climb up Smoking Tree Ridge to a cave, steep and narrow with rope-assisted sections.
notes: No ticketUrl: walking track, no single steward.
Bio fixed: unsourced 'sweeping view' removed. Wikipedia lists 5 hours return, 6 km.
Pin is the route midpoint; cave entrance node is -31.56271,159.08812. Boot scrub station applies at the start of southern-mountain tracks.

lord-howe-island-museum.name: Lord Howe Island Museum
lord-howe-island-museum.bio: Island museum with history from 1788, World Heritage displays and a giant horned turtle skeleton.
notes: Entry by donation (Wikivoyage only) so marked free; official page states no charge. Confirm on the day.
Hours from the island directory; Wikivoyage lists 9AM-3PM. Exact June-August hours not found.
Visitor Centre is in the foyer (separate hours). No Wikipedia article, so no wiki field.

lagoon-beach-lord-howe.name: Lagoon Beach
lagoon-beach-lord-howe.bio: A calm lagoon shore on the island's east side, lined with banyans and pandanus.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach, no single steward.
No wiki field: 'Lagoon Beach' is a generic title and no Lord Howe article was confirmed.
Low confidence: only incidental mentions. Banyans and pandanus come from Wikivoyage's description of the lagoon front, not this beach specifically; recheck the pin against the lagoon's east side.
No Commons photo; needs a search outside Commons.

held.name: Erscott's Hole
held.reason: Owner call: LOW pin confidence (single iNaturalist geotag at -31.54639,159.06083; sources place it off the airport or at a groyne). Not researched for the pin. Known facts: staghorn coral garden, fish conditioned to glass-bottom boats; Lord Howe Environmental Tours 2-hour glass-bottom boat tour A$85 adult with optional snorkel; Wikivoyage spells it Escott's Reef. Official page: https://lordhoweisland.info/natural-attractions/natural-treasures/erscotts-hole/. No Commons photo passes.
